## [1] "country"   "continent" "year"      "lifeExp"   "pop"       "gdpPercap"
summary_table <- data %>%
  group_by(continent) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_lifeExp = mean(lifeExp, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_lifeExp   = sd(lifeExp, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_gdp     = mean(gdpPercap, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_gdp       = sd(gdpPercap, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

summary_table

The above is the summary of life expectancy GDP/continent

lifeexp_plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x = continent, y = lifeExp, fill = continent)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Life Expectancy by Continent",
    x = "Continent",
    y = "Life Expectancy"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

lifeexp_plot

anova_model <- aov(lifeExp ~ continent, data = data)
summary(anova_model)
##               Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F)    
## continent      4 139343   34836   408.7 <2e-16 ***
## Residuals   1699 144805      85                   
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
TukeyHSD(anova_model)
##   Tukey multiple comparisons of means
##     95% family-wise confidence level
## 
## Fit: aov(formula = lifeExp ~ continent, data = data)
## 
## $continent
##                       diff       lwr       upr     p adj
## Americas-Africa  15.793407 14.022263 17.564550 0.0000000
## Asia-Africa      11.199573  9.579887 12.819259 0.0000000
## Europe-Africa    23.038356 21.369862 24.706850 0.0000000
## Oceania-Africa   25.460878 20.216908 30.704848 0.0000000
## Asia-Americas    -4.593833 -6.523432 -2.664235 0.0000000
## Europe-Americas   7.244949  5.274203  9.215696 0.0000000
## Oceania-Americas  9.667472  4.319650 15.015293 0.0000086
## Europe-Asia      11.838783 10.002952 13.674614 0.0000000
## Oceania-Asia     14.261305  8.961718 19.560892 0.0000000
## Oceania-Europe    2.422522 -2.892185  7.737230 0.7250559
gdp_plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x = gdpPercap, y = lifeExp)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "GDP vs Life Expectancy",
    x = "GDP per Capita (log scale)",
    y = "Life Expectancy"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

gdp_plot
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

lm_model <- lm(lifeExp ~ log10(gdpPercap), data = data)
summary(lm_model)

#Results The ANOVA test revealed which pairs of countries had significant differences between their GDPs and life expectancy. These countries include: Americas-Africa, Asia-Africa, Europe-Africa, Oceania-Africa. When plotted using a linearalized regression, it shows that countries with high GDPs have a strong relationship to high life expectancies as well.

#Discussion Countries with higher GDPs may have more money to put towards access to resources that will improve life expectancy. Since the data set uses national averages, it may not represent disparities within countries. No, the statistical significance only tells us that there is a significant between the values in the data set. However, it does not represent if the GDP actually has a large biological effect on the quality and length of life. Country population may bias the data set. Countries with larger populations will have more data.
